provenance: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24117v1 (Raja et al. 2026, 'Grading the Narrators: An Isnād–Rijāl Framework for Claim-Level Provenance in Multi-Agent Knowledge Systems')
text: Multi-agent knowledge systems can grade each narrator's integrity and precision, with weakest-link quarantine: the loop found the unreliable narrator it was given enough evidence about and silently missed the one it was not.
Context poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash patterns; context quarantine, pruning, summarization, and offloading techniques are catalogued for agent context engineering.
Sub-agent context isolation ('context quarantine'): clean context windows that return condensed summaries; workers receive less context than the parent, not more.
Isolate work in dedicated threads, each with its own window (Breunig's 'context quarantine').
A model graded 'Unreliable Narrator' scores strongest on fluency and weakest on coverage — narrator confidence and narrator coverage are different axes.
